Germany

Alcohol and Germans; this is a bit deeper and you don't get more fun out of Germans than drinking with them. It's deeply ingrained in their culture and their cure for hangovers is solid.

Let’s dive into this.

CV

Experience matters, CV style reference: Germans are abusing beer for centuries or even millenia. Some say it is an accepted addiction problem turned into culture (They even have a word for this: „Volksdroge", engl. "drug of the people").

Germans being Germans, loving beer and laws, developed norms to ensure their drug of choice is like they want it to be. The „Reinheitsgrebot“ (purity order) of 1516 is a German norm to brew beer by using water, barley and hops only. No additives allowed. The German point of view: If it is not brewed according to the "Reinheitsgebot" it is not beer and can not be marketed as such.

In Germany it is common to print this on the labels as a sign of quality:

„Gebraut nach dem deutschen Reinheitsgrebot von 1516“ (Brewed according to German purity order from 1516).

Katerfrühstück (Tom Cat Breakfast)

The usual breakfast after drinking alcohol and enjoying yourself is called "Katerfrühstück" (literally: tom cat breakfast, origin see below).

A "Katerfrühstück" usually consists of pickled fish like Bismarckhering (a pickled herring, named after the first chancellor of unified Germany Otto von Bismarck) and pickled vegetables like "saure Gurken" (pickled cucumber or pickled gherkin, a gherkin is a variety of cucumber but smaller), some eat raw (uncooked) "Sauerkraut" (sour cabbage) like the cliché demands.

A combination of pickled fish and vegetables in one dish is called "Rollmops", which is a pickled herring rolled around a pickled cucumber/gherkin. Very tasty.

Besides getting minerals back from the pickled and salted food after peeing more often while drinking, the main reason the pickled food approach works, is because the pickled fish and vegetables make you thirsty and you drink more water or other fluids when eating pickled food. This makes the "Katerfrühstück" an indirect method to force yourself to rehydrate your body.

Konterbier (literally: Counter Beer, engl. "Hair of the dog")

The method of drinking more alcohol to minimize a hangover is called "Konter-Bier" (counter beer, like counter strike) or Konterschnaps (counter schnapps) depending on which alcoholic beverage you use to delay the hangover all the while you are dehydrating even more. In Austria hair of the dog is called „Reparaturseidl" (repair beer or patch beer). Drinking cultures, what do you expect.

Origin of the name "Katerfrühstück"

„Kater" is the German word for tom cat or a male cat, which is used in everyday language to describe a hangover. A hangover is also called „Katzenjammer" (cat misery), but this term is a bit outdated. I don't know why cats play an important role in a hangover, some say it is derived from „Kotzen" (english: puking) or „Katharr" (english: catarrh) which are somewhat similar pronounced.

And that, my friends, is a short overview of Germans catering to their addiction and trying to cope with the inevitable hangover.

More German Alcohol Culture
